name: Left communism in China
summary: Chinese left communism, in its best-documented form, is the ultra-left of the Cultural Revolution, which held that a new bureaucratic 'Red capitalist' class had taken over the party-state and had to be overthrown. It demanded that the old state machine be smashed and replaced by Paris Commune-type organs of mass power, with officials paid like ordinary people and recallable at any time. It rejected the Soviet road and the Revolutionary Committees, while remaining within a Maoist vocabulary.
scope: Represents the Cultural Revolution ultra-left of 1966-68, centered on Shengwulian in Hunan and Yang Xiguang's 'Whither China?' (January 1968), plus the Wikipedia account of the self-described 'ultra-left' and the 'bourgeois right' critique. Excludes Chinese Trotskyism, early Chinese anarchism, and post-Mao writers, which the sources I opened do not detail. Most statements outside class, state, revolution and religion are unaddressed in these texts and are answered at low confidence.

sources.author: Tony Cliff
sources.usedFor: Reading of the text as anti state-capitalist, Commune state with standing army abolished.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ultra-left saw money exchange and distribution by work as persisting bourgeois right to be restricted, so markets allocating resources is alien to it.

public-ownership.rationale: Assumes social ownership of industry as the socialist baseline, but its demand is for who controls it (the masses, not bureaucrats), so formal public ownership alone is not endorsed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Calls for the redistribution of assets and power and for smashing the old order; private property as an overriding right is the opposite of this program.

strong-leader.rationale: Opposed the dictatorship of the bureaucracy and demanded cadres be dismissed at any time by the masses, rejecting rule by a strong leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Wanted the old state smashed but replaced by a Commune-type state and an armed mass dictatorship, so not stateless but not accepting the state either.

limit-guns.rationale: Complained that workers were disarmed and endorsed arming the left and an armed citizenry, so strict gun limits cut against it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Says the army and police became tools suppressing the revolution and demands the standing army be abolished or radically changed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Aimed at a revolutionary break with the old order and disliked inherited ideas; culture preservation is not among its concerns.

gradual-change.rationale: Rejects peaceful transition and reformism, insisting revolution is one class overthrowing another by force and that the state machine be smashed utterly.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Internationalist but views imperialism as failing; no stated role for international bodies such as the UN, so mild inference.

nation-first.rationale: It is class-based and internationalist in outlook, and ignores nationalism, though it uses the term People's Commune of China.

revolution-justified.rationale: Whither China? endorses armed seizure of power and says the bureaucratic dictatorship must be overthrown by force.

experts-over-public.rationale: Calls for mass supervision of cadres and for senior cadres to step aside, rejecting rule by officials or experts above the masses.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Opposes privilege passing to the new ruling class; inheritance taxation is not specifically discussed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The bureaucratic state is the enemy class; adherents would not entrust investment to it without mass control.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wants collective control, not small-owner capitalism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are absent from the sources.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Shanghai ultra-left opposed absorption of independent worker demands into state-sanctioned bodies, rejecting top-down class collaboration.

one-party-rule.rationale: Calls for a revolutionary party of the advanced proletariat but doubts the party under its current leadership and demands mass control over it; not support for single-party rule by an elite.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Radical communism rejects hereditary rule, and the text condemns feudalism.

democracy-best.rationale: Calls the goal mass dictatorship rather than democracy, but wants mass democratic control by Commune-type power; it rejects liberal democracy while demanding popular rule.

direct-votes.rationale: Commune-type mass power and dismissal of cadres by the masses point to direct popular decision-making, though referendums are not mentioned.

workers-councils.rationale: Calls for political organs of the Paris Commune type in place of the existing state, and compares Shengwulian to the soviets of 1917.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nationalities and secession are absent from the ultra-left texts I read.

natural-rulers.rationale: Directly opposes a ruling class of cadres and demands equal treatment with the masses.

political-violence-never.rationale: Endorses armed mass dictatorship and force to overthrow the bureaucratic dictatorship.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mocks religious thought; a Marxist movement rejects scripture-based law.

class-struggle-history.rationale: States that revolution is one class overthrowing another and that struggle continues against a new Red capitalist class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Demands cadres receive the same treatment as ordinary people and attacks high salaries and privileges.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Opposes bourgeois right and material privilege; a communist ethic of collective struggle.

duties-before-rights.rationale: It demands democratic rights and control for the masses over officials; subordinating rights to duties echoes bureaucratic demands for obedience.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy does not appear in Cultural Revolution ultra-left writing, and a Marxist outlook does not settle it.

restore-past-order.rationale: It seeks continuous revolution and condemns the restoration of old hierarchies via the revolutionary committees.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marxist and productivist; no primitivist current.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Sees distribution by work and the wage grades as bourgeois right to be restricted, pointing toward distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Critiques money exchange and bourgeois right persisting under socialism, implying production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Argues the Red capitalist class lives by exploiting the masses through privilege; classic profit theory is not detailed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Calls for an armed mass dictatorship over the bureaucratic class.

collective-farming.rationale: Supports a peasant movement but gives no stated view on collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Treats imperialism as going downhill toward debacle; war causation not argued.

taxation-theft.rationale: Marxist; the state is to be replaced, not tax per se rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: It endorses armed dictatorship over the bureaucratic class, which goes beyond restricting only harm to others.

conscription.rationale: Calls for abolishing the standing army and arming the people.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Emphasizes mass voice and control over leaders.

state-as-business.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.

reviewHistory.rationale: Rejects hierarchy and bureaucracy and wants officials paid like the masses; the customer-citizen model is a market logic it opposes.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

positive-liberty.rationale: Material conditions and power over production are central; not explicitly argued.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a theme; real power is attributed to the bureaucratic ruling class.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marxist egalitarian outlook rejects genetic hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Rejects hierarchical cooptation in favor of Commune-type power from below with recall.

national-rebirth.rationale: A class movement not centered on national decadence; it speaks of revolution against a bureaucratic class.

territorial-expansion.rationale: It denounces imperialism, and a proletarian-internationalist group would not endorse expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Opposes cadre privilege and personal loyalty hierarchies.

bound-labor.rationale: Calls the new order feudal-like and supports peasant movements.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The ultra-left texts are political, not epistemological, and Marxists differ on whether knowledge is class-bound.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora questions do not appear in the sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Mass democratic control over production through Commune power.

rule-by-example.rationale: Demands recall and mass control rather than trusting rulers' morals.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Hostile to religious thought but no stated epistemology.

class-collaboration.rationale: Insists on class struggle against the Red capitalist class and rejects reformist compromise.

dominated-front.rationale: Whither China? invokes anti-imperialism as past struggle but proposes no front of dominated countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Its project is class-based revolution against a domestic ruling class, with proletarian internationalism as background, not nationally bounded labor.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Calls the existing state an apparatus of a ruling class to be smashed and replaced.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theories about immigration contradict its class analysis of power, though the topic is absent from the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary electoral systems are not its concern.

national-mission.rationale: It denounces imperialism and treats the Soviet model as a warning; spreading one's own state form is not its stance.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes cadres as a privileged Red capitalist class living on high salaries and exploitation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Whither China? demands a sweeping social revolution and an armed mass dictatorship, the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts egalitarian internationalism; the sources never raise it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Its demand that officials receive the same treatment as masses rests on equality of persons.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Whither China? warns against the Soviet road, but I found no passage on whether socialism can last in one country.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions do not appear in the sources.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious-based bans are alien to its hostility to religious thought.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Demands smashing the state, though does not discuss the encirclement doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Cadres removable at the masses' demand, but consent theory is not framed.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts class solidarity and Marxist egalitarianism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Whither China? says the bureaucratic dictatorship must be overthrown by force and endorses armed seizure of power.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Its theory is class struggle and mass solidarity, not competition between individuals or peoples.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Opposes bureaucratic domination, though this republican concept is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: Wants unified Commune-type power rather than checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Calls for a revolutionary party of advanced proletarians but distrusts the existing party and favors mass initiative; Cliff also notes Mao's party attacked as privileged class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Aims for the masses against a privileged class.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Shanghai strikers' demands were suppressed as economistic; adherents oppose such restrictions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: It locates oppression in the Red capitalist class, not demography.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Class-internationalist; the claim is foreign to its framework.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Victims of repression; but endorses revolutionary dictatorship.

party-controls-media.rationale: Group was denounced and suppressed; wanted mass voice.

party-commands-army.rationale: Wanted the army united with the masses and its tool role ended.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cadres would receive the same treatment as the masses; Commune precedent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: It wants a revolutionary party of advanced elements but distrusts the existing party and favors mass initiative.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Opposes concentration of command in one person; wants armed masses and abolition of standing army.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hostile to religious thought and rule by unelected authorities.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Cadres dismissable by the masses at any time.

recall-officials.rationale: New cadres may be dismissed or changed at any time according to the masses' demands.

people-in-arms.rationale: Backs arming the left and workers' militias and abolishing the standing army in favor of armed people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: It backs the peasant movement but gives no moral praise of rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Its authors were young intellectuals and students, so it would not endorse this broad distrust.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The text mocks religious thought, so religious doctrine in science teaching would be rejected.

constituent-assembly.rationale: It calls for smashing the old state and Commune-type organs; an elected constituent assembly is not its mechanism.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: It demands mass democratic control and attacks bureaucratic dictatorship; trading freedom for growth is the bureaucracy's logic.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: It wants Commune power and recallable cadres rather than a head of state.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Cliff reads the group as treating bureaucratic state capitalism as a global target, and Whither China? warns against the Soviet road, though it does not use the exact label for the USSR.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hostile to religion but proposed smashing the state itself.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Whither China? demands cadres be recallable and equal to the masses, and mocks idol worship.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Cadres are to be dismissable at any time by the masses, so no ruler stands above accountability.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rejects rule by the few; wants Commune power by the masses.

leader-cult.rationale: Criticizes Mao for opposing the Commune; not a personality cult line.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Argues a new Red capitalist class arose in socialist China and must be overthrown.

land-redistribution.rationale: Backs a peasant movement and redistribution of assets.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy questions of this kind do not appear in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist class analysis of the new bureaucratic bourgeoisie.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The text frames imperialism as a system heading for collapse, so rule by a 'more advanced' society over others would be rejected as imperialist.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-imperialist; cultivating influence over former possessions is imperialism by another name for this outlook.

delink-world-market.rationale: The text names imperialism as an enemy but proposes no policy on trade ties, so this stays neutral.

minority-veto.rationale: Wanted decisive revolutionary action by the masses and mass dictatorship, not consensus procedure where one dissenter blocks.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Endorses force against a bureaucratic ruling class, but the constitutional-law framing is foreign to it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Wanted Commune-type organs replacing the state machine, not parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics does not appear in the ultra-left texts.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal ethics does not appear in the ultra-left texts.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The ultra-left treated privilege as the mark of an exploiting class and demanded abolition, not benevolent duty of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Its whole project was mass political action, the revolutionary seizure of power from the bureaucracy.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The sources focus on bureaucratic power, not cultural reproduction of domination.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The text stresses force and mass dictatorship rather than analyzing how rulers win consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mentions imperialism as an old enemy but offers no world-system analysis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Internationalist class politics but not specifically addressed.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development policy is outside what the sources say, though Maoist self-reliance was in the background.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial claims are not part of its program; class struggle is.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: It claimed the Paris Commune model as of general validity.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Says the army became a tool for suppressing revolution and calls for it to change radically; the group opposes a guardian army.

office-by-exam.rationale: Wants officials removable by the masses; expert-selected officialdom is the bureaucracy it attacks.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Cadres in the Commune order may be dismissed or changed at any time in accordance with the masses' demands.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Cliff links the group against both capitalist and state-capitalist bureaucracy; the Soviet-style intervention into allies is the Soviet road it warns against.

democratic-peace.rationale: Treats imperialism as the world order; democratic-peace theory is a liberal thesis it would not hold.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not set out a doctrine on sovereignty and intervention.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy against a minority is incompatible with Marxist class analysis.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The group demanded mass supervision of officials, which presupposes access to information.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Opposes hierarchy and imperialism; also warns against copying the Soviet model.

defeat-communism.rationale: The group is communist; hostility to this goal is built in.

religion-illusion.rationale: The text derides religious thought and belief in idols, in the Marxist tradition.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Commune model is a mass state, not a network of small communities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The group is communist and claims the true socialist goal; third ways are rejected.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts leftist historical outlook; not directly discussed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The group was itself suppressed; though advocating dictatorship over class enemies.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialist: calls imperialism a system going downhill.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not applicable; religious obligation conflicts with its Marxism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious criteria for legitimacy conflict with its Marxism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Shengwulian drew on the Paris Commune for mass democratic control by ordinary people in work and politics.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The sources focus on class domination by bureaucrats without discussing intersecting oppressions.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It defined itself as further left than the Maoist leadership; left and right are central.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Mocks religious thought; authority comes from the masses.

social-market-economy.rationale: Treats distribution by work and money exchange as bourgeois right to be restricted.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Cliff notes the group proposes a Paris Commune type of state with the standing army abolished.

rich-first.rationale: Attacks bureaucrats' privileged position; rejects inequality that goes first.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Rejects privilege and demands recall of cadres by the masses.

property-franchise.rationale: Mass democratic power; the opposite of a property-based franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism does not appear in the sources.

reification.rationale: The sources do not use Lukacs-style theory, though Marxist critique of commodity relations overlaps.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Believed power lies with a ruling class; the argument about press ownership is not explicit.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Hostile to religion's control over private life.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Critique of privilege and concentration of power in the Red capitalist class.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Wanted the existing state apparatus smashed; the replacement of police is not described.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rebel Red Guards were youth but organized outside official discipline.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Its critique concerns privilege; but distribution by work was itself called bourgeois right.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Endorses armed struggle and armed mass dictatorship.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Class struggle, not spiritual struggle; religion mocked.

culture-before-state.rationale: Priority is political power seizure, state smashed first.

independent-unions.rationale: Shanghai workers sought independent demands against official absorption; no stated union policy.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Argues that China under revolutionary committees was not socialist because power lay with the bureaucrats, not the masses.

second-chamber.rationale: The Commune model unifies power, not a bicameral system.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Commune concept resembles delegated administration but the text calls for a People's Commune of China as a whole.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Class, not race, is the organizing principle.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Whither China? demands the old state machine be smashed utterly and replaced by Commune-type organs, a position no current statement captures.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Internationalist and anti-bureaucratic, but the Maoist framework also endorsed revolutionary wars, so this is not clearly settled.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Anti-imperialist, but the texts look to revolution rather than reform of international economic rules.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Whither China? demands real mass power through Commune-type organs and recallable officials, and says elections held under a new privileged class do not amount to popular rule.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Its call to smash the Red capitalist class and its state rests on abolishing private ownership, so first-come private appropriation of land is rejected.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: A Marxist ultra-left treats religion as ideology to be superseded, so inerrant scripture is not accepted.

national-church-status.rationale: Marxist egalitarian socialism gives no church legal precedence.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Whither China? attacks the privileged bureaucratic class and demands that officials be paid like ordinary workers, so equality of outcome matters more than how holdings arose.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Whither China? analyses exploitation by a new ruling class in Marxist terms, resting on labour as the source of value, though it does not state the theory explicitly.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Whither China? condemns the 'Red capitalist' bureaucratic class and the party-state apparatus, and demands Paris Commune-type power, so party-led markets are rejected.

police-more-powers.rationale: Says the army and police became tools suppressing the revolution and demands the standing army be abolished or radically changed. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Anti-imperialist; cultivating influence over former possessions is imperialism by another name for this outlook. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: The existing state machinery should be smashed and replaced, not taken over and used.
missingStatements.rationale: Whither China? demands the old state machine be smashed utterly and replaced by Commune-type organs, a position no current statement captures.

notes: Many answers are low-confidence inferences because the ultra-left texts concern class power, the state and the army, not social or foreign policy. Chinese Trotskyists or anarchists would answer differently, e.g. on vanguard parties.
